title: Book your movers

researchPrefs.question: What matters most when you choose a mover?
How flexible is your move date?
Which items need the most attention?

desc: Get binding estimates from three USDOT-licensed movers. Book 8-12 weeks out for summer moves, 4-6 weeks off-season.
tips: Get a binding estimate — federal law caps your final bill at 110%.
whyNeeded: Booking late means leftover dates, leftover crews, and leftover quality.

title: Book your cleaners

researchPrefs.question: What matters most when you choose a cleaner?
How much cleaning do you need?

desc: Schedule a move-out deep clean for the day after your movers finish. Get three quotes and confirm scope in writing.
tips: Insist 'inside appliances' is in writing — most charge extra otherwise.
whyNeeded: One missed area can cost you your entire security deposit.

title: Rent your moving truck

researchPrefs.question: What matters most for your truck rental?
How fixed is your pickup time?
What is your main truck concern?

desc: Compare U-Haul, Penske, and Budget on size, mileage, and total cost. Reserve 4-6 weeks out — earlier in summer.
tips: Size up if borderline — one trip always beats two.
whyNeeded: Late means the wrong size, wrong pickup location, or no truck at all.

title: Schedule internet install

researchPrefs.question: What matters most for your internet service?
When do you need service working?

desc: Protect your first workday from an outage: order service 2-3 weeks ahead, confirm exact-address availability, and ask whether self-install is available.
tips: If your home is pre-wired, compare self-install timing and current fees with a technician appointment.
whyNeeded: Without it, you're tethering work calls to your phone for days.

title: Sell what you're not bringing
desc: List on Facebook Marketplace, OfferUp, or Craigslist 4+ weeks out. Drop the price 10-20% every three days until it sells.
tips: Post photos in natural daylight — listings sell twice as fast.
whyNeeded: Every unsold item becomes a box you pay to move.

title: Schedule donation pickup

researchPrefs.question: What matters most for removing these items?
How soon do the items need to go?
What makes up most of the load?

desc: Book a free pickup with Salvation Army or Habitat ReStore 3-4 weeks out — peak season wait times stretch to a month.
tips: Get an itemized receipt at pickup — it's a tax write-off.
whyNeeded: Last-minute, you'll be hauling furniture to the curb yourself.

title: Handle your vet
desc: Update your address if staying. If switching, request vaccination records, lab results, and any chronic-care notes for your new vet.
tips: Get the rabies certificate separately — boarding facilities require it on-site.
whyNeeded: Without records, boarding kennels and ER vets may turn you away.

title: Forward your mail
desc: Keep important mail from landing at your old address: file through the official USPS change-of-address page and verify the start date and household members.
tips: Marketing mail and magazines don't forward — update senders directly.
whyNeeded: Anything sent to your old address — bills, tax docs, checks — vanishes.

title: Request your time off
desc: Request 2-3 days minimum: one for packing, moving day, and one to recover. Submit at least four weeks ahead.
tips: Block the day after move day — unpacking always runs longer than expected.
whyNeeded: Without time off, you'll be answering Slack with a couch on your back.

title: Update employer records
desc: Update your home address with HR. If you crossed state lines, also update your work-state W-4 — addresses and taxes are tracked separately.
tips: Confirm payroll updated 'work state for taxes' — addresses don't sync.
whyNeeded: Wrong state withholding turns next April into a W-2 nightmare.

title: Cancel your utilities
desc: Schedule shutoffs for electric, gas, water, sewer, and trash. Set the date for the day after you move out, not the day of.
tips: Give them your forwarding address — credit refunds arrive by mail.
whyNeeded: Utilities running in your name after move-out keep billing you.

title: Set up new utilities
desc: Call electric, gas, water, and trash providers 2-3 weeks ahead. Schedule activation the day before you arrive — overlap beats outage.
tips: Get a 'letter of credit' from your old utility — waives the deposit.
whyNeeded: Arriving at a dark, waterless house ruins your first night.

title: Transfer your utilities
desc: Call each provider 1-2 weeks out. Schedule the new address active a day before, the old address shutoff a day after.
tips: Same provider = no new deposit, no credit check, no setup fee.
whyNeeded: Without overlap, you'll lose water mid-clean or power mid-move.

title: Update your child's school
desc: Submit your new address with proof of residency. Update emergency contacts, transportation requests, and pickup authorizations the same day.
tips: Bus zones change at the address level — confirm yours immediately.
whyNeeded: An old address can drop your kid from the bus route overnight.

title: Find your new daycare
desc: Get on multiple waitlists immediately — infant care can take 12-24 months. Tour in person and ask about ratios, licensing, and turnover.
tips: Send a handwritten thank-you after touring — directors remember you.
whyNeeded: Waitlists can outlast your move date by a full year.

title: Update your daycare
desc: Email the director with your new address, updated emergency contacts, and any drop-off or pickup time changes.
tips: Update authorized pickup list in writing — verbal changes don't stick.
whyNeeded: Outdated emergency contacts can block pickup if your child gets hurt.

title: Transfer your pharmacy
desc: Call the new pharmacy with your old pharmacy's name and number — they handle the transfer in minutes for chain stores.
tips: Controlled prescriptions don't transfer — get a new one from your doctor.
whyNeeded: Running out mid-move means an urgent care visit just to refill.

title: Update your auto insurance
desc: Notify your insurer with the new address before move day. Premiums shift by ZIP code — sometimes by hundreds per year.
tips: Get three new quotes the same day — ZIP changes are perfect leverage.
whyNeeded: Wrong address on file can void your coverage in a claim.

title: Cancel your condo insurance
desc: Call your insurer with your move-out date. Schedule cancellation for the day after closing or possession transfer to avoid coverage gaps.
tips: Ask for a prorated refund — most insurers owe you for unused months.
whyNeeded: Cancel too early and a last-day flood becomes your problem alone.

title: Cancel your renter's insurance
desc: Call your insurer to cancel — most do it online in 5 minutes. Schedule the end date for the day you hand back keys.
tips: Ask for the unused premium back — you're owed a prorated refund.
whyNeeded: Canceling before key return leaves your stuff uninsured during the last load.

title: Set up condo insurance
desc: Get an HO6 policy effective on closing day. Read the HOA master policy first — it determines whether you need walls-in or full coverage.
tips: Ask the HOA which master policy type — bare walls, walls-in, or all-in.
whyNeeded: The wrong HO6 leaves your floors and cabinets unprotected after a leak.

title: Set up homeowner's insurance
desc: Lock in coverage 2-3 weeks before closing. Lenders require a paid first year and proof of binder before they'll fund the loan.
tips: Quote at least three insurers — premiums vary 30%+ for identical coverage.
whyNeeded: Without an active binder at closing, the deal stalls and your move with it.

title: Set up renter's insurance
desc: Protect your belongings and satisfy lease requirements: compare current coverage and terms from licensed insurers, then bind a policy for move-in day.
tips: Bundle with auto insurance — usually saves 5-15% on both.
whyNeeded: One pipe burst can wipe out your belongings without coverage.

title: Transfer your condo insurance
desc: Call your insurer 2-3 weeks ahead with the new address. Verify the new HOA master policy type — coverage needs may shift.
tips: Different HOAs = different coverage needs — re-quote, don't just transfer.
whyNeeded: An assumed transfer can leave gaps your old policy covered automatically.

title: Transfer homeowner's insurance
desc: Call your insurer 3-4 weeks before closing. Premiums shift with location, age, square footage, and roof — get a new quote either way.
tips: Re-quote three insurers — transfers rarely beat fresh-quote pricing.
whyNeeded: A 'transfer' often hides a premium increase you'd catch by shopping.

title: Transfer renter's insurance
desc: Call your insurer with the new address 1-2 weeks ahead. Transferring keeps your claims-free discount and skips the new policy fee.
tips: Ask for the multi-year loyalty discount — most insurers don't volunteer it.
whyNeeded: Restarting fresh resets discounts you've spent years earning.

title: Scan your home
desc: Pan your camera slowly across each room. Peezy's AI identifies furniture, appliances, and large items in about 20 seconds per room.
tips: Open closets and cabinets — Peezy catches what you'd forget to mention.
whyNeeded: An accurate inventory unlocks precise quotes and protects you against damage claims.

title: Defrost your freezer
desc: Empty the contents, unplug it, prop the doors open, and lay towels underneath. Plan 24-48 hours before move day.
tips: After moving, let it sit upright for 4 hours before plugging back in.
whyNeeded: Movers won't load a wet or leaking fridge — full stop.

title: Deep clean the place
desc: Plan 6+ hours with two people. Hit appliances, baseboards, walls, windows, vents, and cabinets — landlords inspect every one.
tips: Clean inside the oven and fridge first — they're the top deduction trigger.
whyNeeded: One missed area can cost you hundreds in deposit deductions.

title: Do the final touch-up
desc: After everything is out, walk every room, closet, and cabinet. Wipe baseboards, sweep floors, and confirm nothing is left behind.
tips: Bring a flashlight — corners and closets hide more than you think.
whyNeeded: A forgotten item or dusty corner is exactly what landlords cite.

title: Cancel homeowner's insurance
desc: Call your insurer once the sale closes. Set the cancellation date for the day after closing — never before.
tips: Ask for the prepaid premium refund — most owe you for unused months.
whyNeeded: Canceling early voids coverage during the final walkthrough and key transfer.

title: Update your license address
desc: Bring your current license and two proofs of new address to the DMV. Most states require updates within 30 days.
tips: Check your state — many let you update online without an appointment.
whyNeeded: An outdated address can void traffic ticket service and jury duty notices.

title: Handle the new-state DMV
desc: One DMV trip covers it: new license, and vehicle registration if you drive. Most states give you 30 days after the move.
tips: Request REAL ID — TSA needs a new one in your new state.
whyNeeded: Driving past the deadline on an out-of-state license is a moving violation.

title: Reserve move-out access
desc: Lock in truck parking — and the service elevator if your building has one — before move day.
tips: Reserve two adjacent spots — trucks need ramp clearance too.
whyNeeded: No reserved access means movers burn paid hours hunting for parking.

title: Reserve move-in access
desc: Lock in truck parking at the new building — and the service elevator if there is one — before the truck arrives.
tips: Ask the building to cone off the spot the night before.
whyNeeded: An unreserved elevator is the #1 cause of movers' overtime charges.

title: Protect your deposit
desc: Photograph the empty unit, return every key and fob, and keep the record — your deposit's evidence file.
tips: Shoot video too — it captures context photos miss.
whyNeeded: Without proof, deductions are your word against theirs.

title: Handle the school transfer
desc: Notify the current school, request records, and start enrollment at the new district — one parental job, one card.
tips: Many districts let you start enrollment paperwork online before you arrive.
whyNeeded: Enrollment gaps cost kids school days.

title: Move your medical records
desc: One pass across your providers — records requested, addresses updated, transfers started.
tips: Call the front desk — most offices send records electronically in days.
whyNeeded: New providers can't treat you safely without your history.

title: Handle your money accounts
desc: Banks, cards, brokerages, loans — one pass updates every address so autopay and statements never miss.
tips: Update before your next statement closes — mismatches trigger fraud alerts.
whyNeeded: Outdated info triggers fraud alerts and frozen cards on day one.

title: Handle your memberships
desc: Gyms, studios, spas, clubs — cancellations and transfers need 30-day notices. One pass, all of them.
tips: Check your membership terms — some require 30 days written notice.
whyNeeded: Miss a notice window and you pay for a gym you can't visit.

title: Choose your storage unit

researchPrefs.question: What matters most when you choose storage?
When do you need the unit?
What is your main storage need?

desc: Avoid sold-out or inconvenient storage: compare current, sourced options near your new place, then confirm availability and terms directly.
tips: Reserve early, and confirm every promotion and move-in term before paying.
whyNeeded: Sold-out units near the new place mean storing across town.

title: Add your new address
desc: Your plan is waiting on the destination. Add it and everything downstream unlocks.
tips: A street address beats a city — distance and deadlines get exact.
whyNeeded: Distance, deadlines, and half your tasks depend on where you're headed.

title: Lock in your move date
desc: You marked the date flexible. Lock it in — or confirm the estimate — so the plan paces itself right.
tips: Mid-month weekdays book cheaper movers than month-end weekends.
whyNeeded: Every deadline on your plan counts backward from this date.

title: Lighten the load?
desc: Move less and lower the packing load: choose what to sell or donate, then use a step-by-step plan for each item.
tips: Every unsold item becomes a box you pay to move.
whyNeeded: Selling and donating both need lead time — the earlier we know, the more it pays.

title: Need a storage unit?
desc: Know before move day whether it all fits — and what a unit near you actually costs.
tips: Units near new builds sell out first — early answers get options.
whyNeeded: Waiting until move day can leave only inconvenient or unsuitable options.

title: Tell us how moving day went
desc: Protect your own record of moving day: capture arrival, pace, final price, and damage while details are fresh.
tips: Stick to what happened — arrival, pace, price, and damage.
whyNeeded: Fresh facts give you a clear record for reviews, claims, or disputes.

title: Return or recycle your boxes
desc: Reduce waste and improve future kit estimates: count what left your home, then choose a local donation, reuse, or recycling option.
tips: Flatten clean boxes before donation or recycling, and keep wet or damaged cardboard separate.
whyNeeded: Returned counts reduce waste and make the next kit estimate sharper.
